scope: 600 measured compiler builds + 180 Rust/ZIL native runtime rows independently recalculated; direct ZIL runtime-quality arithmetic belongs to a separate review.
All 100 associated unscored compiler preflight rows, saved native binaries, startup/warmup and per-build oracles checked.
No original runner import or aggregation call; block means, median of block means, weighted absolute costs and ratio implemented here.
Per-case/request intervals, all-27 resampling support, geometric paired-block ratio and leave-one-case-out are additional descriptive sensitivities, never replacement scores.
Three paired blocks do not establish a product gate or general performance superiority.
Bridge has source/object caches and query disabled; Rust incremental has query enabled. No pooled score.
Recorded CT usage and cache/preflight accounting checked; logs do not expose all internal budget decrements and this review is not a full budget-semantics proof.
Extracted ctime/path differ by design; original identities checked for internal consistency, actual bytes and POSIX modes matched directly to original tar.
Rust/LLVM SDKs are not retained in this artifact; their frozen hashes, versions and original toolchain receipts are checked for consistency, not freshly re-executed.
Old 22.93% result is not migrated. Host model, CPU affinity, source and block count differ; changed host does not establish a causal explanation of performance.

archive_transport.note: Root reclaimed the 68 MB duplicate gzip during the first review read after another independent archive check, causing a transparent read interruption. The replacement xz carries the unchanged tar stream; all members were independently reread here. This transport incident is not a CI/measurement failure.

conclusions: Within this host/window, bridge weighted wall is 0.8879857% lower and every block aggregate is below one; gain is small and not universal across cases.

Bridge cold and unchanged request intervals cross one; private/public intervals are below one. tree4x2 compile is slower in all three block aggregates; retained point estimate is slower with an interval crossing one.
O0 Rust cold is effectively tied in the main weighted estimate, interval crosses one; two of three block ratios and the paired geometric sensitivity exceed one. No confirmed overall Rust lead.
Rust incremental is 20.0135% slower in wall and 43.3699% more CPU; unchanged/private/public are slower in all three blocks. Cache-enabled first builds are a distinct request and are slightly faster.
O2 closed complete compile is 9.6820% slower than Rust, with all three aggregate block ratios above one; improved runtime quality must not be called compile-time superiority.
Rust comparisons remain faster for small cases but largest-tree compile is slower in every main Rust window; removing that case is a diagnostic sensitivity, not a replacement result.
O0 native runtime weighted lead is dominated by tree1024x8; tree4x2 remains slower than Rust. O2 native runtime weighted ratio is about 0.97985, with tree4x2 about 1.01080.
No old 22.93% number, no bridge/query-enabled incremental pooled score, and no formal product gate follows from these three blocks.
